title: Six weeks to stay
speaker: tenant_salmah
dialogue: This cloth has passed through three generations of hands, you know. Now the new lease wants more than double the rent. I can teach someone the trade, but if I cannot afford the shop, how to teach? What would you protect first?
question: Keep traders in place, invest in their skills, or build community ownership?
options: Buy tenants time, with owner compensation.
Support apprenticeships; this does not directly reduce rent.
consequence: Rent protection improves affordability; it does not permanently end rent pressure. A skills grant improves continuity but cannot substitute for affordable premises.
visual: Focus the Arab Street parcel. Use its existing affordability condition; do not claim an individual eviction unless a future individual-shop model tracks it.

title: The empty apprentice’s stool
speaker: custodian_rahim
when: Later round when continuity < 0.45, unless lineage is already broken
dialogue: The tools are still here. But who is going to learn to use them? A photo can keep the pattern, sure. The feel of the hand, that one you must learn from someone. How do we give this trade a future?
question: Support transmission of skills, protect premises, or find a new use?
options: Reduce the pressure that makes staying difficult.
Support a new use with an archive protection clause.
consequence: Grants directly support continuity. Reuse improves activity and equity, but its annual affordability penalty can undermine living trades.
visual: Use the lineage-trades parcel condition. An empty stool is a proposed narrative prop, not an existing animated asset.

title: A street everyone visits
speaker: operator_jo
when: Later round with vitality > 0.70 and affordability < 0.50, or MONOCULTURE
dialogue: People come to Haji Lane for the independent shops. Their spending keeps our staff working, lah. But if every landlord only chases the tourist crowd, how will the small businesses stay? Some of that success should come back to the neighbourhood, right?
question: Keep growing visitor activity, redistribute its benefits, or protect tenants?
options: Raise community capacity and equity, with a ten-year sunset.
Expand activity, accepting wider social and heat costs.
consequence: Higher vitality can intensify rent pressure. If MONOCULTURE is active, that stronger pressure persists even after the mix improves.
visual: Compare visitor-economy activity with Arab Street occupancy indicators; do not equate a busy street with a healthy district.

title: Whose night is it?
speaker: tenant_salmah
when: Any round when considering night-economy expansion
dialogue: I understand why the food stalls want to stay open later. They have families to feed also. But our working day starts early, you know. If the street stays noisy all night, the people upstairs how to sleep?
question: Expand the evening economy, improve daytime access, or invest in cooling?
options: Negotiate a noise curfew before expansion.
Improve walking and shade while retaining delivery access.
Improve habitability without directly expanding activity.
consequence: The curfew softens the night policy’s habitability and equity penalties and reduces its immediate vitality boost. It does not remove the continuity penalty.
visual: Night lighting is proposed. Existing board activity and conditions can already show the calculated trade-off.

title: The afternoon nobody stays
speaker: operator_jo
when: Later round with habitability < 0.40, or HEAT_LOCK
dialogue: Around the Malay Heritage Centre and Sultan Gate, walking should be part of the visit. But so hot, people need shade and somewhere to rest. Our shops still need deliveries also. Can we make these streets work better for the people using them every day?
question: Cool existing buildings, redesign the street, or raise money first?
options: Add shade and walking space with a morning loading window.
Raise capacity, without directly repairing heat conditions.
consequence: HEAT_LOCK halves positive habitability recovery and adds a vitality penalty. Cooling is more effective before the threshold is crossed.
visual: Use the existing shade corridor and tree-health changes; heat shimmer and crowd avoidance remain proposed.

title: Who gets to belong?
speaker: youth_faiz
when: Later round with equity < 0.35, or EXODUS
dialogue: Around Sultan Mosque, people come to pray, work and meet one another. Visitors are welcome, of course. But the neighbours must still feel this is their place also. Can visitor income and affordable space help the next generation stay involved?
question: Change ownership, share visitor income, or invest in learning?
options: Support community ownership of nearby premises.
Redistribute visitor gains and raise capacity.
Support skills with a smaller annual equity benefit.
consequence: Once EXODUS has triggered, equity cannot rise above 0.50 in this model. Later improvements do not automatically rebuild lost networks.
visual: Highlight residents and makers, then show the actual equity condition and irreversible flag.

title: New keys, old walls
speaker: custodian_rahim
when: Any round when considering adaptive reuse; use when later-round vitality < 0.40
dialogue: I am not saying every room must stay exactly the same, lah. A building needs a use. But when the new business moves in, what will it remember? Is there still room for the old work inside?
question: Change the building’s use, invest in its trade, or cool it for everyday use?
options: Accept an archive protection clause and its added cost.
Improve habitability; this does not directly create economic activity.
consequence: Archive protection adds immediate continuity and costs six capacity. It does not cancel the reuse policy’s annual affordability penalty.
visual: Use the existing continuity and vitality conditions. A detailed before-and-after interior is proposed.

title: The pattern no one can teach
speaker: custodian_rahim
when: Later round with LINEAGE_BROKEN; highest narrative priority
dialogue: The tools, we can keep. The records also. But a record cannot teach you, right? Some of the knowledge is already gone. What can we protect now, even if we cannot bring everything back?
question: Support remaining knowledge, protect remaining tenants, or sustain public space?
options: Support surviving practice, within the recovery limit.
Improve conditions for people who remain.
consequence: LINEAGE_BROKEN caps annual continuity recovery at 0.003. A grant still has its immediate effect; the flag is never removed.
visual: Show the flag and its actual trigger year on the receipt. Do not describe a grant as restoring a vanished lineage.

title: Space to make something
speaker: youth_faiz
dialogue: Aliwal Arts Centre gives us a place for the arts. But joining in takes time and affordable space also. Young people need to believe they can stay nearby. Can we make room for artists and residents, not just the visitors who can pay?
question: Share visitor income, support community premises, or fund the next generation?
options: Support community ownership of nearby premises.
Redistribute visitor gains and raise capacity.
Support skills with a smaller annual equity benefit.
consequence: Once EXODUS has triggered, equity cannot rise above 0.50 in this model. Later improvements do not automatically rebuild lost networks.
